entities.name: Thibaud of Ostia
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Thibaud of Ostia, also known as Theobald, was a highly influential French cardinal-bishop of Ostia and Velletri who served the Papacy during a tumultuous period of the late 12th century, dying on November 11, 1188. A trusted diplomat and jurist, his career spanned the pontificates of Pope Alexander III and Pope Lucius III, placing him at the nexus of major ecclesiastical and secular conflicts, most notably the protracted struggles with Emperor Frederick I Barbarossa and the complex preparations for the Third Crusade. His unwavering commitment to papal supremacy and his extensive legatine missions across Western Europe made him a central figure in defining the Church's role in medieval politics and international relations.

Elevated to the cardinalate by Pope Alexander III, Thibaud quickly distinguished himself as a formidable papal legate. He played a crucial role in the negotiations that culminated in the Peace of Venice in 1177, which resolved the two-decade schism between Alexander III and Frederick Barbarossa, effectively ending imperial anti-popes and reaffirming papal authority. Prior to this, he presided over the Third Lateran Council in 1179, a landmark synod that standardized papal election procedures requiring a two-thirds majority for cardinals and condemned various heresies like Catharism. Throughout the 1180s, Thibaud was instrumental in diplomatic efforts across France and England, striving to reconcile King Philip II Augustus and King Henry II, a critical prerequisite for a unified response to Saladin's capture of Jerusalem in 1187.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Thibaud of Ostia was a pivotal papal legate and cardinal whose diplomatic and legal work significantly strengthened papal authority against imperial challenges and laid crucial groundwork for the Third Crusade. His contributions to the Third Lateran Council reforms had a lasting impact on Church governance.
